Apple has a lot to launch this fall, with the highlights being the iPhone Ultra and iPhone 18 Pro unveiling next month. Apple is also busy preparing a new iPad mini, and reports today suggest it will arrive in October.

The new iPad mini is on the way

In the latest edition of the Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman reports that the new iPad mini with an OLED display "should go on sale by the end of October."

This suggests the new iPad mini won't be announced at next month's "Surprise and shine" special event, but is more likely to be unveiled by Apple separately in October, either through a press release or another dedicated event.

Here's a recap of the expected updates for the new-generation iPad mini:

  • OLED display
  • Improved performance, expected to feature the A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip
  • A "redesigned enclosure" with better water resistance
  • A全新的震動式揚聲器系統

This is the first iPad mini update in two years. Apple last refreshed the device in October 2024, when it added the A17 Pro chip, Apple Pencil Pro support, and Apple Intelligence compatibility.

The iPad mini's pricing went up by US$100 earlier this year, from US$499 to US$599. Amazon currently has it on sale for US$569. Whether the new model will see another price hike remains to be seen.

Also over at 512 Pixels, Stephen Hackett has written a great piece looking back at the history of the iPad mini and how its role and positioning within Apple's lineup has evolved over time.

I think one of the biggest questions right now is what impact a foldable iPhone Ultra will have on the iPad mini market. The iPhone Ultra essentially offers a two-in-one iPhone plus iPad mini form factor. Will that eat into standalone iPad mini sales? I'm somewhat skeptical, as I think a lot of people prefer to keep their iPad and iPhone separate.

Are you considering buying the new iPad mini? What are your thoughts on Apple's smallest iPad form factor? Drop us a comment and let us know.
